answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the nebula schedule in the comet ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ember checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 133 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 12 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
